Report concisely: (1) does the Twitch.Player JS API offer getCurrentTime, seek, play/pause, getEnded, and events like READY/PLAY/PAUSE/ONLINE/OFFLINE/ENDED? (2) does it support live channels, VODs and clips? (3) requirements: `parent` domain, HTTPS, minimum player size; (4) any rule about drawing things over / obscuring the player, or other content restrictions. Quote short phrases where relevant.

Embedded video windows must be at least 400x300 pixels. There are three types of VODs: * _Past broadcasts_ are created automatically from a live stream. * _Highlights_ can be created by broadcasters from past broadcasts. * _Uploads_ are external videos that are added to Twitch using the Video Uploads API or the Video Manager. This guide discusses three techniques for embedding video and clips * Embedding live streams and VODs in a [non-interactive frame](#non-interactive-inline-frames-for-live-streams-and-vods). * Embedding live streams and VODs in an [interactive iframe](#interactive-frames-for-live-streams-and-vods). * Embedding [clips](#non-interactive-iframes-for-clips) in a non-interactive frame. For more information, see [Video on Demand](https://help.twitch.tv/s/article/video-on-demand) and [How to Use Clips](https://help.twitch.tv/s/article/how-to-use-clips) . Non-Interactive Inline Frames for Live Streams and VODs ------------------------------------------------------- ### Iframe Attributes These attributes are defined in the IFrame element. The Twitch player can not set or modify them. | Name | Type | Description | | `allowfullscreen` | boolean | A boolean attribute set by inclusion. In other words, including the attribute enables fullscreen viewing while excluding the attribute ensures fullscreen viewing is not allowed. | | `height` | number or string | Height of the embedded window, in pixels. This can be expressed as a percentage as well, by passing a string like `100%`. Minimum: 300 | | `parent` | string | **Required.** Domain(s) that will be embedding Twitch. You must have one parent key for each domain your site uses. | | `src` | string | The iframe `src` URL string should be [https://player.twitch.tv/](https://player.twitch.tv/) with one of these required query string parameters:

`channel` – (string) Name of the channel, for a live stream.

`video` – (string) Video ID (for past broadcasts, highlights, and video uploads). In this context (the video player), the video ID must have a “v” prefix.

`collection` - (string) Collection ID, for a collection of videos.

If both `video` and `collection` are specified, the specified collection starts playing from the specified video. If the video is not in the collection, `collection` is ignored and the specified video is played.

If `channel` is specified along with `video` and/or `collection`, only `channel` is used. | | `width` | number or string | Width of the embedded window, in pixels. Embedding Twitch/Embedding TwitchNavigation menu:Embedding Twitch/Embedding Twitch

Embedding Twitch
================

Bring Twitch live video, video on demand, and chat into your own website

Copy as markdown[View as markdown](/docs/embed.md)

[Provide feedback for this page](https://github.com/twitchdev/issues/issues/new?template=documentation-bug-report.md)

Introduction
------------

You can embed Twitch functionality in your website in three ways:

*   [Embedding Everything](/docs/embed/everything/) explains how to embed both the video player and Twitch Chat for live content or video on demand in one iframe. This includes the functionality for _follow_, _subscribe_, and _login_.
*   [Embedding Chat](/docs/embed/chat/) explains how to embed just Twitch Chat.
*   [Embedding Video and Clips](/docs/embed/video-and-clips/) explains how to embed just the video player, including Clips.

Embedded Experiences Requirements
---------------------------------

The use of any Twitch embeddable experience must comply with the requirements below and the Twitch Developer Services Agreement. Twitch may revoke embed usage for domains that are not in compliance. Twitch reserves the right to revoke your ability to use our embeddable experiences, for any reason, at any time.

1.1 Domains that use Twitch embeds must use SSL certificates.

1.2 Twitch requires our embed users to verify where they use our products on the web using a special parameter: `parent`. Depending on your integration method, you may provide this as a query parameter in an iframe `src` attribute, or as a property on the JavaScript object you use to construct a new Twitch embed. For more information, see the embed API documentation above and our initial announcement of the requirement. Embed domains that don’t specify this parameter will trigger a playback error message that will direct end users to click through to Twitch if they wish to watch that content.

1.3 Embeds must utilize only Twitch-approved player elements and should not be obscured in any way by other page elements in whatever domain context they may appear. Certain features, such as the ability to send chat messages, may be disabled if the iframe is obscured or not visible.

1.4 Embeds must adhere to the minimum height and width requirements outlined in their respective attribute tables.

Providing Feedback
------------------

We’re constantly trying to improve the developer experience, so if you encounter any difficulty using Twitch embed, please provide feedback via [Embed Feedback](https://link.twitch.tv/embed-feedbackform).

*   [Introduction](#introduction)

content.text:
**(1) JS API (Twitch.Player)**
- **getCurrentTime**: yes, but only for VODs, not live streams. Described as "Works only for VODs, not live streams."
- **seek**: yes, `seek(timestamp:Float)` in seconds. "Does not work for live streams."
- **play / pause**: yes, `play()` and `pause()`.
- **getEnded**: yes, returns true if the live stream or VOD has ended.
- **Events**: all six exist, registered with `addEventListener(event, callback)` as `Twitch.Player.READY`, `.PLAY`, `.PAUSE`, `.ONLINE`, `.OFFLINE`, and `.ENDED`. The page also lists PLAYING, SEEK, PLAYBACK_BLOCKED, and CAPTIONS.

**(2) Content types**
- **Live channels**: yes, via the `channel` parameter.
- **VODs**: yes, via `video`, with a "v" prefix on the ID (e.g. `v40464143`). Collections are also supported.
- **Clips**: yes, but only through a non-interactive iframe at `clips.twitch.tv/embed?clip=<slug>`. The page says it "does not support the JavaScript interactive embed," so there is no playback API for clips.

**(3) Requirements**
- **parent**: required on the iframe. The JS docs say it is only needed when the site is embedded on domains other than the one that instantiates the player. The embed intro says domains without it "will trigger a playback error message."
- **HTTPS**: "Domains that use Twitch embeds must use SSL certificates."
- **Minimum size**: the intro says embedded windows "must be at least 400x300 pixels." The attribute tables give a minimum width of 400 and a minimum height of 300 (for clips, 400 and 300 as well). Autoplay also needs the minimum size and visibility.

**(4) Obscuring and content rules**
- Rule 1.3: embeds "should not be obscured in any way by other page elements in whatever domain context they may appear." Some features, such as sending chat, may be disabled if the iframe is obscured or not visible.
- Rule 1.3 also says embeds "must utilize only Twitch-approved player elements."
- Twitch may revoke embed usage for non-compliant domains, and the intro points to the Twitch Developer Services Agreement, which I did not read.
- The docs have no rule that names overlays specifically. However, "in any way" appears to cover drawing captions or other graphics over the player, so an overlay like that would likely conflict with this rule.
